notes.title: Epiphany (and new test branch version)
notes.notes:
Just had a major moment of realization thanks to the people doing the Chinese translation, and it might fix this ancient problem with anti-virus programs corrupting saves. I was saving variables as both strings and binary to the save files (*GAM), depending on variable type. This made it impossible to open saves with notepad.

The latest test branch [u]now saves and loads everything as a string[/u], and the saves are now plain text that can be edited with notepad. As a bonus, somehow the files are smaller. I used to think notepad couldn't open saves because they were too big and notepad was too stupid. Now I know better, and I'm gonna update Warlord with this soon also.

I still haven't had time to install anti-virus programs and test if they still fuck it all up, but I do know that now translators and modders can edit the *.GAM save files with notepad and search+replace whatever words or item descriptions they want.

I also included 4 new commands to edit the HUD labels for "Chapter", "Respect", "Info", and "(none)". All the globals.bsl scripts now have those 4 extra commands to set the HUD labels.

Gonna keep this update in test branch for another week or so to make sure nothing gets fucked up. To opt in to the test branch, right-click Brigand in Steam, go to Betas tab, and choose "Test" from Beta Participation. If you have a save that you are working on or attached to, back it up or just don't opt in to the beta.

It does take a couple extra seconds to save and load (because it has to convert variables to strings and back), but it makes modding so much easier, and I have a food feeling anti-virus programs will not fuck with my game or my brain anymore, so it's worth it.

New version is up. There have been a LOT of fixes, but I still haven't had time to work on the performance issues or the crashing issue that are problems on some computers. Hopefully those will be addressed in version 3.9B next weekend. Apparently there is also a problem with the Strength stat resetting itself and Ricardo's dialogue resetting when you visit him later, but I haven't been able to recreate these bugs yet.

Here's a complete list of changes and fixes:

SOURCE CODE:
-Tweaked slope movement penalties.
-Fixed problem with thrown object targets in the HIT scripts.
-Fixed problem with script "if" statements when no object is selected.
-Increased animation speed for the "playObject" command (for traps in the upcoming DLC).
-Added new script command, "if_tag=none" to test if there is no currently-selected object.
-Added option in GUI world editor between 5x5 elevation and 5x5 smooth elevation.

SCRIPTS:
-Fixed damage type for explosive barrels and gas tanks.
-Increased gas tank explosion radius from 100 to 150 (same as conc grenades).
-Glaives, cinder blocks, etc. will now automatically break if they hit stone or metal.
-Fixed bug where cancelling Thunder's pistol shop with the discount would sell you a Thumper.
-Fixed game-breaking bug during Chapter 5 siege where a thug would be moved inside a solid building.
-Changed rag "uses" description from "infinite" to "disposable" in INIT script.
-Fixed bug where the player piano in Junk Fort wouldn't decrease UBNS respect.
-Changed "Strait of Panama" to "Panama Canal" in dialogue and texts.
-Improved some item descriptions for flavor in the INIT scripts.
-Doubled Strength skill bonus of banana beer from 5 to 10.
-Added new script for world editor: "makeHouse.bsl".
-Fixed a bit of inconsistent dialogue.

RESOURCES:
-Changed world map on Junk Fort monitor and in Player's Manual.
-Replaced fall sounds with something more realistic ("thump1.wav" and "thump2.wav").

STORY FILE: (requires starting a new game)
-Improved the first map a little (Ricardo's Plantation).
-Changed rag "uses" description from "infinite" to "disposable" in story file.

notes.title: New Patch on Friday (or Saturday)
notes.notes:
There are some new bug reports (and some old complaints) that I'll try to fix before Saturday. There are probably some new script problems that arose after I changed the assets folder system for modability.

Also there are some slowdown and crashing issues on some computers. The low FPS and crashing problems are unrelated, but I'll work on both of them.

EDIT: The game will crash on some computers if you load too many maps (and hence images) in one play session without quitting. So the temporary solution is to quit and reopen the game after you save to prevent crashes. Most computers don't have this problem, but I'll try to fix it in the next patch (or the one after).

notes.title: Version 3.8
notes.notes:
Version 3.8 makes the world editor a little easier to use with some new commands and GUI options that allow you to easily edit the ground tiles so you don't need to manually edit the corners and edges of grass, mud, etc. You can also edit the ground and cliff elevation more smoothly, now.

Mostly I just did it for myself, so I can finish the Panama DLC faster. My goal is to eventually make the world editor as user-friendly as the Starcraft map editor.

I also fixed a bug in which the map corner planes would appear black underwater, and I think I improved performance in the map scripts slightly.

notes.title: Version 3.7, Framerate Increase
notes.notes:
Yeeeaahh, I fixed the framerate slowdown on some computers, I think. I was playtesting on high game speed (46 FPS), and noticed the game slowed way down when walking on ground or cliff terrain on crowded maps. This has been fixed, so everything should be much smoother now.

I also added a bunch of performance options before I made this discovery. You can now run the game in 16-bit color, turn down the draw distance, and turn down the rain effects (so that the rain completely stops when you are indoors, so there's no need for raindrop collision). But honestly you probably won't need these new options now that I fixed that aforementioned slowdown bug. I need your feedback with all your own computers and video cards.

Also some other minor bugs were fixed (check updates text).

notes.title: Version 3.6
notes.notes:
The most important bug fix was that thrown items would not run their hit scripts if they were past their throw peak and falling (i.e. throwing a poison axe sometimes wouldn't poison your target). That's been fixed.

Poison Blade and Eleggua's Curse abilities now require a target, just like the Gun Smith ability, rather than bringing up a list. This is so I can add more weapons that you can poison/curse in the DLC. I also made it possible to curse plates, trays, cinder blocks, and microscopes (anything you can throw you can now curse). The cursed hit animations also look a bit better now.

I also fixed a couple of script oversights, improved some text, and prevented items from being thrown off the map. Here's a complete list.

SOURCE CODE:
-Fixed bug in which thrown items wouldn't run hit scripts if falling, after throwing peak.
-Improved weapon gluing to limbs for characters who are attacking a bit (still not perfect).
-Changing the volume option in the menu now instantly turns down environment sounds that are still playing.
-Prevented items from being thrown off the map (and getting out of reach).
-Decreased map AI range a bit (the last update made it a bit too slow).

SCRIPTS:
-Added new flavor text to Chapter 1 opening depending on the player's chosen class (speculations about why they framed you).
-Changed Poison Blade and Eleggua's Curse abilities to require a specific target for a weapon, rather than selecting from a list.
-Added the option to use Eleggua's Curse ability on plates, trays, microscopes, pipes, and cinder blocks (so they cause cold damage).
-Improved HIT script for cursed melee and thrown weapons, showing new animation and sound.
-Fixed bug in which you could only bring Ricardo a batch of coca leaves one time.
-Fixed bug in which UB Mercs would get bloody after one point of damage.
-Fixed some melee weapon INIT scripts to correct grip limb positions.
-Fixed Harbinger Sniper INIT script to fix a texture problem.

RESOURCES:
-Added cursed textures and icons for cinder blocks, plates, trays, pipes, and microscopes.
-Removed more duplicate objects from the OAXACA assets folder, making the total file size smaller.
-Made the toilet flushing sound quieter.
-Improved a couple of textures.

STORY FILE: (requires starting a new game)
-Fixed Harbinger Sniper drawing priority in story files (to fix texture).
-Fixed some melee weapon grip limb positions in the story files.

notes.title: Version 3.5
notes.notes:
Fixed a bug where the player wouldn't automatically obtain coins from corpses if there's another item sitting on top of it, so now it should be easier to make some more money. Also, I deleted a lot more duplicate assets. The total file size is down to under 800 megs now. Lots of other little fixes, so look at the Updates txt for a complete list, as always.

I've started working on the Panama DLC. I've made a few new character skins and I have a bunch of new objects, but I don't wanna give anything away this early. It will still be a couple of months before it's finished.

notes.title: Version 3.4B + Future Plans

I just did a quick update to fix a couple of bugs, one where all the Subz Juicers would disappear in the Scumlands before the player can fight them, and another one where the wrong Chapter 2 loading screen shows up (there are two completely different second chapters). Also, I added a unique face icon for Fluffy the dog.

There's gonna be another patch before the end of the month, not sure when. I'm making the world editor easier to use, not for you people, but so I can encourage myself to make a bit of new content without wasting so much time. If there are any more suggestions or bugs, please let me know.

notes.title: Version 3.4
notes.notes:
Major update with 3.4. I redesigned the entire Assets folder so that game stories will look for the assets in the special story folder first, then look in the default folder as an alternative. This means that I deleted a lot of duplicate files so the game is now less than a gig, and also it will be easier to make new stories (you don't have to copy the entire default assets folder anymore). This should encourage me to make another challenge map some time in the near future. The next update will include more world editor improvements.

I also fixed a problem with the last update that slowed the player down when moving on terrain, and I made enemies' heads explode with enough damage on a head shot.

Another important change is that I gave more Voodoo skill to the Witchdoctor class (but less Willpower). This is because it's hard to find a Voodoo trainer early in the game.

Here's a complete list of fixes:

SOURCE CODE:
-Redesigned asset folders so that story folder takes priority, other use default folder (eliminating the need for duplicate files).
-Fixed bug from the last update which caused the player to move more slowly on the ground terrain matrix.
-Fixed bug in which muting volume in game launcher would disable map loading music, even after turning volume back on.
-Fixed a rare bug in which teammates would transfer to map with player but leave the team.
-The "NewStory" command now gives you the option of creating a new empty assets folder.
-Targets' heads now explode if dealt enough damage and killed in a head shot.
-Decreased slope speed penalties, especially moving downhill.
-Decreased cliff sliding damage, increased free fall damage.

SCRIPTS:
-Fixed bug where Carmen would still teleport outside the Polyphonic if the entire team leaves.
-Fixed bug in which beers would sometimes leave you with another beer instead of an empty can (though the texture would change).
-Fixed bug in finale in which McVannon would talk to you prematurely while you're on the top floor.
-Fixed bug where one of the backup rowboats on the oil platform spawns sticking through a wall.
-Decreased Witchdoctor starting Willpower from 30 to 25 and increased Voodoo from 10 to 15.
-Added one final isopod demon respawn on Freeway 200 in Chapter 10.
-Gave Gao 10 Pistols skill because he starts with a pistol (init script).
-Increased Zac's Voodoo from 10 to 20 for player training (init script).
-Made Cortez's initial dialogue exit automatically in BRIGAND - FORTRESS.

RESOURCES:
-Eliminated most duplicate asset files, greatly reducing file size.
-Improved textures: "plaster" and "plasterB" (starting cell).
-Added nighttime cliff and ground textures for map corners.
-Updated Brigand Builder's Manual.

STORY FILE: (requires starting a new game)
-Changed texture of loose dirt in the Scumlands so it's not the same as the ground texture.
-Gave Gao 10 Pistols skill because he starts with a pistol (story file).
-Increased Zac's Voodoo from 10 to 20 for player training (story file).
-Improved Freeway 175 map a bit.

notes.title: Version 2.8
notes.notes:
Version 2.8 of Brigand is up, which makes the game a little easier. There are more save points and helpful items, but only if you start a new game. Also, I fixed a bug that prevented the player from scoring head shots. The player can now score head shots on almost all baddies, doubling the damage -- don't worry, ONLY the player can score head shots. I also fixed a bug that prevented teammates from reloading their gun if they had a melee weapon. Finally, I increased the damage of the Shorty AR and the Harbinger Sniper, just because they are so expensive. These things will make the game slightly easier, because I do want a few more people to beat it.

I also improved the GUI of the world editor a bit and allowed quick saving when using the world editor mode (F3). That means if you REALLY want to save scum, play the world editor mode and press F3 to save at any time (you no longer need to type any commands). Also, there are some small aesthetic improvements, as well as a compass object that you must now use to activate the HUD compass. The compass is easy to find.

There are still 3 known bugs that I can't seem to fix, but they are very rare and minor. Hopefully the next update will fix all known issues once and for all. You can check out the update text in the game folder for more info.

I never got around to fixing that slow-down problem if there's a baddie under the docks trying to kill you in Loma Larga (next time), but I did make a few significant improvements.

notes.title: Version 2.2 + New DLC
notes.notes:
Version 2.2 is up, along with the new DLC I promised so long ago. It's not really DLC, since it's included with the game now. This is because I want an example alternative story file so people can learn how the world editor works.

Just start a new game and choose the new story file, BRIGAND - FORTRESS.

It is only one map in which you must defend a SIMDA relay for 3 days and 3 nights (one hour in real time). When the baddies are attacking, you can complete side jobs, hire muscle to help you out, activate automated security systems, scavenge for items, and explore the area for vantage points.

This is meant to be a possible demo for a future paid DLC called Brigand: Panama, but it will be quite a while before that comes out, and also I need some people to help me with new character textures. Thanks to Unmutual for helping me out with the texture for Officer Cortez.

Warning: the third and final night is extremely hard.

notes.title: Version 2.0
notes.notes:
I finally got the new version up and everything seems to be working. I would back up your save file if you have one, though, as the sub-directories have all changed to accommodate for multiple story files. It's probably fine, but better to be safe.

Included is a save converter, so if you want to continue your character from version 1, run that program first on the launch menu, select your character, and wait a few seconds.

Major changes include a new World Editor launch option. The world editor could still use some work, but you can play around with it and start creating your own stories. I still have to implement a way to upload files, but it will probably be a while before any content is ready anyway. I was planning to have a free example DLC story with this release, but that will have to wait a week or so. It will be a single-map defense challenge.

As for bug fixes, the upside-down texture bug is no more. The solution was so simple that I now spit at my reflection in the mirror every morning for not fixing it earlier. I also increased the max objects per map from 2000 to 5000, so feel free to hoard as many guns and beers as you want on any map -- it won't crash the game.

There's a whole lot of other fixes, too. Check the Brigand Updates text file in the game folder to see everything that's been updated.

notes.title: Plans for 2.0 (release: Halloween)
notes.notes:
I've been busy with real life lately, but I will start work on v2.0 this weekend and hopefully finish by the end of October. Here is a list of the planned improvements, but I am always open to more suggestions:

1) Most importantly, there will be a new World Editor launch app, which will be like the main low-res game app, but it will allow you to open two editor modes: GUI and a command prompt. You can edit anything while you play, including maps, dialogue scripts, AI, etc. You can also erase the entire game and build your own story from scratch, importing any models you want. You can then save your new story file for others to download and play.

2) The max number of objects per map will be increased from 2000 to 5000. The game currently crashes if the player hoards too many items on one map. This improvement will require larger save files, so old saves will not be compatible.

3) A few new menu options, including one to increase the frame rate from 33 to 66. These new menu options are another reason old saves will not be compatible.

4) Hopefully I will fix the bug where textures flip upside-down. I have a new version of the compiler which fixes it, but it doubles the loading times and causes a couple other problems, so I may just add another launch option if I can't fix it in the current compiler version.

5) There will be bloodstained textures for injured characters.

6) A simple challenge story file to demonstrate the World Editor functionality.

Please give me more suggestions. I can't promise they will be implemented by Halloween, but I can try.

I wish I could start introducing more features, but like my mom always told me, "Son, when you are patching a game on Steam, you need to make sure the main story campaign is free of bugs before you start adding new features." I always took that advice to heart.

So lots of script bugs are fixed, you can check the update file as always.

I plan to release another patch on Labor Day weekend, version 1.9, which should hopefully finish fixing all the script bugs. I might end up just getting drunk and having sex at the beach, though, so fuck all y'all.

When I get to 2.0, however, that's when the world editor, free DLC, and user-made content page go up. So 1.9 will hopefully be the last patch for the main story file. I am still working out the details for the user-made content, making sure it won't fuck with the other user-made content. I am thinking of other old games where this would happen constantly.

notes.title: Version 1.7
notes.notes:
Damn it! I was drinking at the bar with students, then I came home and started arguing about politics on Facebook. Never argue about politics on Facebook.

Anyway, I'm releasing the new version because some important bugs were fixed, including one that gave you the bad ending only if you specifically went for the good ending. It should be fine now.

There is a host of other script bugs yet to be fixed, and I swear it's not just because I'm an incompetent alcoholic. Brigand's story is complex as fuck. I'll release 1.8 on Sunday with more script fixes. 

Thanks again to all play testers who stomped their way through this swamp. I hope you at least had fun killing shit.

It seems like the guy who beat the game and got the bad ending due to a script bug had tons of fun anyway, so fuck it.

notes.title: Version 1.4, Future Plans
notes.notes:
I fixed the problem of the cursor going off-screen on dual monitors. I know most people who play this game are hard-core nerds with dual monitors. The cursor still goes off-screen in dialogue windows, etc., when the cursor is visible. I think it should be much more playable, but I can't really test it myself.

I also fixed a couple other things. Check the txt for details.

Finally, future plans:

There should be a free demo up on Steam later this week, which is limited to 2 areas only (out of over 20). It will be able to play DLC, as long as it is only 2 maps.

Speaking of DLC, there will be some free DLC stories in a week or so. The world editor will come in a couple weeks, and users will be able to upload their own story files, import their own resources, etc.

notes.title: Version 1.2
notes.notes:
Just put up the second update, fixing lots of script bugs that prevented some side objectives from being completed, thanks to Hedoroman1, who has been blasting through the game faster than I ever thought possible. There was also one corrupt voice file which crashed the game in Chapter 8, which is now fixed.

More importantly, I fixed the bug that caused the text in text windows to flash on some video cards, making it unreadable and making the game unplayable. The problem was changing font color. I removed the font color changes in the windows.

Finally, I think the problem with dual monitors is fixed. The cursor used to cross over to the other monitor, which also made the game unplayable. I do not have dual monitors to test this, but I think it's fixed. Please let me know, all your nerds with dual monitors.

Unfortunately, I was not able to fix the worst bug of all, which makes the text windows unreadable on some Radeon video cards. I need access to a computer that has this problem for a couple hours to fix it. I know one guy with such a laptop in the local area and I should have the problem fixed this week.
